nodes.name: Summer sunlight
nodes.desc: Long northern summer days power a short, intense growing season for the plants of the valley and the alpine slopes.

nodes.name: South Nahanni River and meltwater
nodes.desc: The river and its tributaries run the length of the reserve and water the willow thickets, sedge meadows and river flats.

nodes.name: Wildfire
nodes.desc: Fire is a normal part of boreal forest. It recycles nutrients and opens ground for shrubs and berries.

nodes.name: Soil and limestone minerals
nodes.desc: Thin northern soils, built on limestone in much of the region, hold the nutrients that plants draw on.

nodes.name: Fungi and bacteria
nodes.desc: Break down dead plants and animals, returning nutrients to the soil.

nodes.name: Grayleaf willow
nodes.desc: A common shrub willow of the reserve, browsed by moose, hares and Dall sheep and used by beavers.

nodes.name: White spruce
nodes.desc: A main tree of the boreal forest in the valleys. Snowshoe hares gnaw its twigs and bark in winter.

nodes.name: Cowberry
nodes.desc: A low evergreen berry shrub. Its fruit is eaten by bears and foxes, and caribou eat the plant.

nodes.name: Low northern sedge
nodes.desc: A grass-like sedge of open ground, eaten by Dall sheep and ground squirrels.

nodes.name: Reindeer lichen
nodes.desc: Pale ground lichens that are winter food for caribou and, where the ground is bare of snow, Dall sheep.

nodes.name: Moose
nodes.desc: A big browser of willow and other shrubs. Its carcasses feed wolves, bears and scavengers.

nodes.name: Dall sheep
nodes.desc: Lives on steep alpine slopes, eating grasses, sedges and willow, and lichens in winter. Wolves, bears and golden eagles prey on it.

nodes.name: Woodland caribou
nodes.desc: Eats lichens, plus plants such as cowberry. The reserve is thought to hold two herds, a species at risk in Canada.

nodes.name: Snowshoe hare
nodes.desc: Eats willow and other woody twigs in winter and is the main prey of lynx. A key food link in the boreal forest.

nodes.name: Arctic ground squirrel
nodes.desc: A burrowing squirrel of open tundra and meadows that eats sedges and other plants. Eagles and bears hunt it.

nodes.name: American beaver
nodes.desc: Cuts willow and other woody plants and dams streams, making ponds.

nodes.name: Canada lynx
nodes.desc: A cat that specialises in snowshoe hares and is listed among the mammals of the reserve.

nodes.name: Red fox
nodes.desc: Hunts hares and other small prey and also scavenges carcasses and eats berries.

nodes.name: Common raven
nodes.desc: A scavenger that feeds on carcasses left by wolves and other predators.

nodes.name: American black bear
nodes.desc: An omnivore of forest edges that eats berries and also takes hares, beavers and young or dead ungulates.

nodes.name: Golden eagle
nodes.desc: A bird of prey of cliffs and open country that takes ground squirrels and young Dall sheep.

nodes.name: Gray wolf
nodes.desc: Hunts moose, caribou, Dall sheep and beavers, and its kills feed ravens, foxes and bears.

nodes.name: Grizzly bear
nodes.desc: The reserve is thought to hold around 500 grizzlies. They eat ground squirrels, moose, caribou and sheep, as well as plants.
